items.statement: disconnect_cache rejects the no-flush plus pass-through combination, opens the control device, maps no_flush to flush_data, and submits KCAS_IOCTL_DISCONNECT_CACHE.
The disconnect ioctl resolves the cache ID to a name and passes the pass-through and inverted flush flag into cache_mngt_disconnect_cache, which validates, acquires, quiesces, and stops the cache.
The kernel disconnect path rejects the combination of no-flush and pass-through.
The kernel disconnect path rejects a standby cache with OCF_ERR_CACHE_STANDBY.
The kernel disconnect path rejects an incomplete cache with OCF_ERR_CACHE_IN_INCOMPLETE_STATE.
When flushing is enabled, a running cache is flushed and a flush failure enters cleanup.
Only pass-through disconnect captures exported objects, drains outstanding cache I/O, and purges cache metadata.
Disconnect enables the cache no-dirty state before optional flushing and management locking.
Before stop processing, exported objects are switched to pass-through and their queues are frozen.
After acquiring the named cache reference, each cache-state precondition failure releases that reference before returning.
After a successful stop, the captured pass-through object list is unfrozen when required and then released.
Both userspace and kernel reject no-flush combined with pass-through.
Userspace encodes no_flush as the inverse flush_data flag, and the ioctl boundary inverts flush_data back for the kernel call.
The kernel management boundary refuses disconnect while the acquired cache is in standby state.
The kernel management boundary refuses disconnect while the acquired cache is incomplete.
Cache drain bridges its asynchronous completion callback to an interruptible synchronous wait.
Cache stop runs through a finish thread and may continue asynchronously when the synchronous wait is interrupted.
Userspace maps OCF_ERR_FLUSHING_INTERRUPTED to the INTERRUPTED result.
Userspace reports OCF_ERR_WRITE_CACHE as a failed disconnect with errors.
Userspace reports any other negative disconnect status as a generic failure.
Kernel disconnect cleanup restores pass-through and queue state, releases captured objects and locks, re-enables dirty-data admission, and drops the cache reference as applicable.

items.description: Disconnect first prevents new dirty data and, unless no-flush is requested, flushes a running cache before taking the management lock.
items.statement: cache_mngt_disconnect_cache sets no-dirty before the management lock and, when flushing is enabled, flushes a running cache and aborts through cleanup if that flush fails.
